analysis.title: Cheniere Energy (LNG/CQP): First Take: 3Q26 Miss, but Large 2026 Guidance Raise and Slightly Better 2027 Volume Guide
key_insights: LNG reported 3Q26 adj. EBITDA of $1,900m, below GSe of $1,960m and FactSet consensus of $1,988m (-3%/-4%). Realized volumes and margins were slightly lower than expected.
CQP reported 3Q26 adj. EBITDA of $954m, above GSe of $911m and consensus of $934m (+5%/+2%).

LNG raised 2026 adj. EBITDA guidance to $8.75-9.25b (+10% at the midpoint vs $7.9-8.4b prior), compared with GSe of $8.41b and consensus of $8.36b. The guide implies ~28% upside to GS's 4Q26 estimate at the midpoint.
2026 DCF guidance was raised to $6.05-6.55b from $5.3-5.8b. Management does not typically guide to optimization gains not yet captured.

LNG introduced a 2027 volume outlook of 56-58 mtpa of total capacity (ex-commissioning), slightly better than GSe of 56-57 mtpa. About 52 mtpa is subscribed under long-term contracts, in line with GSe.

About 5 mtpa (250 tbtu) is available to CMI in 2027, of which 4 mtpa is pre-sold and 1 mtpa is unsold. This is at the high end of GSe of 4-5 mtpa, versus revised 2026 of ~300 tbtu and initial 2026 guidance of 150-250 tbtu.
GS sees higher strip pricing versus its price desk as an upside risk to its 2027 estimates. Official 2027 EBITDA guidance should come with 4Q26 results.
CCL Stage 3 is complete, with Trains 5/6/7 reaching substantial completion in March/June/August 2026. Midscale T8 & T9 is now guided online in 2H28 and is 58.6% complete versus 48.3% at 2Q26.

No additional commercial updates came with the release, following last week's QatarEnergy SPAs for 4 mtpa through 2054 and the 0.8 mtpa Petrobras deal announced last month. Focus remains on final SPL T7 permits ahead of an FID by early 2027.
LNG bought back $731m (2.8m shares) in the quarter versus GSe of $500m. CQP's distribution was $0.89/unit versus GSe of $0.82/unit.
Total volumes of 684 tbtu were just below GSe of 687 tbtu and up 2% QoQ on the CCL Stage 3 ramp. LNG EBITDA per unit of volume recognized was 2% below GSe and 1% lower YoY.

GS price targets and estimates are unchanged ahead of the call. Key call topics: drivers of the FY26 guidance raise, the 2027 volume bridge, SPL FID steps, expansion commercialization, global LNG supply/demand into winter, and buyback cadence.

market_movers.rationale: Buy and $308 target (12.5x 2027 EBITDA) unchanged. GS calls the release strong on the FY26 guidance raise, buyback execution and 2027 volume outlook.
Sell and $51 target (12x 2027 EBITDA) unchanged despite a 3Q26 EBITDA beat and a higher distribution.

earnings_insights: LNG 3Q26 adj. EBITDA reported $1,900m vs GSe $1,960m and FactSet consensus est $1,988m (miss of 3.0%/4.4%). Up 5.3% QoQ and 18.2% YoY versus $1,608m in 3Q25.
CQP 3Q26 adj. EBITDA reported $954m vs GSe $911m and consensus est $934m (beat of 4.7%/2.2%). Down 3.0% QoQ and up 7.8% YoY.
LNG 3Q26 dividend reported $0.625/share vs GSe $0.610 and consensus est $0.599. Buybacks reported $731m vs GSe $500m.
CQP 3Q26 distribution reported $0.890/unit vs GSe $0.820 and consensus est $0.803.
LNG raised 2026 adj. EBITDA guidance to $8.75-9.25b from $7.9-8.4b (GSe $8.41b, consensus est $8.36b) and DCF guidance to $6.05-6.55b from $5.3-5.8b.

3Q26 volumes recognized were 693 TBtu in the variance table (GSe 702, +19.3% YoY), volumes loaded 685 TBtu (GSe 694), and cargoes 188 (GSe 197). The text cites total volumes of 684 tbtu versus GSe 687.
risk_factors: LNG downside risks: lower-than-expected global gas prices, higher-than-expected US natural gas prices, execution issues, asset concentration, and a high-multiple fold-in of CQP.

CQP upside risks to the Sell rating: SPL Expansion upside, more favorable SPL Expansion financing terms, better-than-expected marketing flow-through from CMI, and a high-multiple roll-in from sponsor LNG.
